sections.html:
Tuscaloosa sits beside the Black Warrior River in west-central Alabama, roughly 60 miles southwest of Birmingham, and serves as the county seat. The 2020 count was 99,600 residents and the 2025 estimate is 114,288, which makes it the fifth most populous city in the state. The 2020 figure was a 10.1 percent rise from 2010.

Buyers often search by neighborhood, and names that come up include Alberta, Downtown, East Tuscaloosa, Hillcrest, North River, West Tuscaloosa, Central and Midtown, and the University of Alabama campus area. Houses near campus, near the retail corridor around 15th Street and McFarland Boulevard, and along the river can each appeal to a different kind of buyer. Lake Tuscaloosa is wholly within city limits, which shapes lakefront demand.

City hall does not issue the tax bill; county offices do. The Tax Assessor values the property and the Tax Collector bills and collects, both at 714 Greensboro Ave, with the collector in Room 124 and the assessor in Room 108. The collector's main line is (205) 464-8230, and the assessor's is (205) 464-8240.

DateWhat happens
October 1Taxes are due
December 31Last day to pay without penalties or interest; a postmark of that day is accepted
January 1Taxes are delinquent and delinquent notices go out
After March 15Personal checks are no longer accepted
AprilOnline tax sale is advertised, then held in the last week of the month

These dates follow the statewide schedule. Delinquency only gets more expensive with time, so deal with an old balance before you list the house.

sections.h2: How the county values a city house
sections.html:
Values are reviewed on a four-year cycle by the appraisal staff, and they look again in between when a building permit, septic permit, recent sale or taxpayer request triggers it. A recently permitted remodel can prompt a review, so keep the permit paperwork in your sale file.

To protest a value, send a written protest to the County Board of Equalization. Alabama allows 30 days from the written notice of valuation. Call the Tax Assessor's office to learn what it needs with the protest.

Children inside the city limits attend Tuscaloosa City Schools; those outside belong to the Tuscaloosa County School System. The city system has about 10,000 students in 24 schools, including Paul W. Bryant High School, Central High School and Northridge High School. One street over the line can mean the other system, so verify the zone before telling a buyer.

The April 27, 2011 tornado hit Tuscaloosa hard, and parts of the city were rebuilt afterward. Ask yourself when your house was built or repaired, and keep records from that period. Buyers and insurers like to see dates for roofs, siding and structural work. Tree and roof damage from later storms should be documented the same way.

An old balance will not stop you from selling. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff. Your title company uses that number and pays the balance from your proceeds at closing. If a bill was mailed to an old address, confirm your current mailing address with the collector's office so notices reach you.

Take along the deed, a photo ID and your newest tax statement. Where heirs share the house, every owner generally signs, so start that conversation early.

A college town with a storm history produces a few predictable problems.

  • Houses used as student or investor rentals that need turnover repairs.
  • Roof, siding and tree damage from storms, with repair records that buyers may ask to see.
  • Heirs who live out of town and need to settle a family house.
  • Back property tax that went to an old mailing address.

The University of Alabama is the largest employer, so demand follows the school calendar, and Mercedes-Benz U.S. International adds a steady base of workers who need housing. With a cash sale, a title company pays any county tax balance from the proceeds and you avoid waiting on a buyer's lender.

The simplest way to avoid penalties is to pay before the last day of December. A postmark of December 31 is accepted, but a payment that is mailed late or lost in the post can still leave the account delinquent, so mail early or pay in person. Personal checks stop being accepted after March 15, so a delinquent owner who wants to settle later in the spring should plan on another form of payment.

If you sell in the fall, decide in the contract who pays the bill that comes due on October 1. Many sellers pay a share and many buyers take the rest. Whatever you agree, put it in writing and tell the closing agent so the number on the settlement statement is right.

sections.h2: What to bring to the county offices
sections.html:
Come prepared and a visit takes minutes. Bring photo ID, the deed or the parcel number, and your last statement if you have one. If you are acting for a relative who died, bring the death certificate and any court papers that show your authority. The collector handles payment and payoff figures. The assessor handles values, exemptions and changes to the property record, so questions about a remodel or a new addition go to the second office.

If you cannot visit, phone the numbers above and ask what can be handled by mail or online. The county also runs its tax sale online, so the same habit of checking the county site pays off.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the tax year
sections.html:
Listing in late summer or early fall puts the October 1 due date inside your sale window. Listing in winter means the account may already be delinquent, and a delinquent notice goes out in January. Either way, check the balance once at listing and again a week before closing, since a payment can post or a notice can change the number.

If you plan to sell in April or later with a balance still open, remember the tax sale. Parcels with unpaid tax can be advertised that month, which is a poor time to be surprised. A clean payoff in hand keeps you well clear of it.

sections.h2: How a sale works step by step
sections.html:
Start with a payoff request from the Tax Collector and a look at your own records. Next, decide between an agent listing and a direct cash offer. After an offer is accepted, the title company searches the record for liens and unpaid tax, schedules the signing and orders payoffs. At the table you sign the deed, the county is paid from your proceeds and the remainder is yours.

Cash buyers skip the lender appraisal, which often cuts weeks from the timeline. That matters for a rental that needs turnover work or a house with storm repairs a loan appraiser might question.

faqs.q: When are Tuscaloosa property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1. December 31 is the last day to pay without penalties or interest, and taxes turn delinquent on January 1.

faqs.q: Does the City of Tuscaloosa bill property tax itself?
faqs.a: No. The county tax offices bill and collect it. The Tax Assessor handles valuation and the Tax Collector at 714 Greensboro Ave, Room 124, handles payment.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tuscaloosa?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 99,600 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 114,288.

faqs.q: When is the Tuscaloosa County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county advertises it online in April and holds it online in the last week of April.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Tuscaloosa house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A title company can get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector and pay the balance from your sale proceeds at closing.
